As a decorative, unattributed pair, this sits in ordinary estate-auction territory rather than antique-porcelain territory. I have no specific realized comps for this exact unmarked pattern/maker to cite, so I'm not fabricating any; I'm basing the estimate on the general realized range for similar unmarked decorative Chinese blue-and-white gu vase pairs at estate-auction houses (typically $100–350 for a pair), and erring toward the lower-middle of that band given the lack of any mark. Confidence is capped low per the no-maker rule. Restoration is not a relevant lever here since condition appears sound and there is no antique premium to unlock — restored/as-is value should be treated as equal.

appraisal.reasoning: This is a decorative, hand-painted Nippon-era porcelain vase (Morimura Bros importer mark, c. 1911-1921) with typical Art Nouveau-style gilt strap handles and a hand-painted narcissus/cottage-landscape motif — a common decorative genre for the mark, not a rare pattern (e.g., no moriage dragon, no coralene, no beading). Morimura/Nippon marks are plentiful and this style of floral vase with scenic reserve is one of the more commonly encountered forms; I do not have specific recalled realized auction comps for this exact pattern/size to cite, so confidence is capped low per instructions rather than invented. General market experience with this class of Nippon hand-painted vase at estate auctions (EBTH and similar venues) puts realized hammer prices roughly in the $60-200 range depending on size and painting quality, with plainer or smaller examples at the low end and larger, finely painted or rarer-marked pieces higher. Current bidding ($85 across 24 bids with 44 hours remaining) is consistent with this piece landing in the $100-150 range at close, which is where I've centered the as-is estimate. No restoration is evident or warranted; restored value is essentially the same as as-is since condition already appears sound. Given the ordinary (not rare) nature of the pattern and mark, this should be treated as a modest decorative lot, not a standout find — erring toward the lower end of plausible outcomes.
